prompt: Create a historical map showing the expansion of the Roman Republic and Roman Empire around the Mediterranean. Distinguish territory controlled by 264 BCE, 44 BCE, 14 CE, and 117 CE. Label Rome, Carthage, Alexandria, Constantinople, the Mediterranean Sea, and major provinces, with a chronological legend.

spec.title: Expansion of the Roman Republic and Empire around the Mediterranean
spec.subtitle: Territorial Control at Key Dates: 264 BCE, 44 BCE, 14 CE, and 117 CE

sources.title: Cambridge Ancient History: Map of the Roman World in the Time of Augustus
University of South Florida: Roman Power at 264 BCE
University of South Florida: Expansion of the Roman Republic to 14 CE
Barrington Atlas of the Greek and Roman World
Edinburgh University Press: Map of the Roman Empire, c. 14 CE
Provincia Sicilia in the Roman Republic
Les provinces romaines de Sicile et de Sardaigne-Corse

notes: Territorial extents are approximate and based on historical sources.
Client states are labeled for 44 BCE and 14 CE where applicable.
Disputed territories (e.g., Armenia, Mesopotamia) are included in the 117 CE extent but were not always directly administered.
Modern country borders are used for geographic context only.
spec.referenceSummary: This map depicts the expansion of the Roman Republic and Empire around the Mediterranean at four key dates: 264 BCE (First Punic War), 44 BCE (death of Julius Caesar), 14 CE (death of Augustus), and 117 CE (death of Trajan).
